# Ojo Tennis

> Ojo Tennis is a web app for recording, reviewing and sharing tennis matches. You prop an ordinary
> phone at the back of the court and record the whole session, upload it to Ojo, then watch it back
> in a player built for review — scrubbing, frame-by-frame stepping and slow motion. Ojo's AI
> breakdown marks where each rally starts and ends and groups them into service games, so you can
> jump from point to point. Matches are private by default and shareable by a revocable link.

Ojo Tennis is free while in early access. It is not affiliated with any tennis federation, club or
equipment manufacturer.

## What it is for

- Recreational and club tennis players who have never seen themselves play.
- Reviewing a full match (up to ~2 hours) rather than clipping highlights.
- Sending a specific match to a hitting partner or a coach.

## What it does not do

- It does not require a court-mounted camera, tripod rig, subscription hardware or a second person
  to film. A phone at the back of the court is the whole setup.
- It does not keep score, call lines, or produce shot-by-shot statistics.
- It does not publish your matches. Every upload is private to its owner until the owner shares it.

## Key facts

- Platform: web app (any modern browser) plus an iPhone recorder app.
- Recording: landscape, from behind the baseline, one tap for a whole session.
- Upload: chunked, so an interrupted or slow connection does not lose the file. Large matches are
  compressed automatically rather than rejected.
- Review: scrub, single-frame stepping, variable-speed and slow-motion playback.
- Automatic analysis: rally start/end detection, grouped into service games.
- Sharing: private by default; per-match private links that can be revoked; optionally visible to
  players who follow you. A recipient can add a shared match to their own library without
  re-uploading it.
- Price: free during early access.
